What is being evaluated: Demonstrates a clear understanding of the purpose, scope, and importance of the POCSO Act.
Recognizes the importance of safeguarding children from sexual abuse, exploitation, harassment, and inappropriate conduct.
Demonstrates an understanding of the responsibilities of school staff when concerns or disclosures arise.
Shows awareness of the need to respond appropriately to concerns, disclosures, or suspected abuse and follow the school's reporting and escalation protocols.
Demonstrates awareness of appropriate adult–student boundaries, interactions, communication, and conduct.
Understands that confidentiality has limits in safeguarding situations and that information may need to be shared with appropriate authorities/staff to protect the child.
Reflects an understanding of how an adult should respond to a child's disclosure—remaining calm, listening, avoiding judgment or blame, and not conducting their own investigation.
Demonstrates sensitivity to the child's safety, dignity, voice, and best interests when responding to concerns.
Connects POCSO knowledge to realistic school-based situations and demonstrates appropriate professional judgment.
Goes beyond summarizing the Act and reflects on how the learning influences their own responsibilities, behaviour, boundaries, and practice as a Student Champion.
